mcat_description.short: Bunk House Portable Toilets are prefabricated, relocatable toilet cabin units designed specifically for construction site labour camps and temporary worker accommodations, manufactured in FRP, MS, or GI materials with integrated plumbing and sanitation systems.
mcat_description.long: Bunk House Portable Toilets are factory-built, self-contained sanitation cabin units engineered for deployment at construction labour camps, remote project sites, and temporary worker bunk house settlements. They are manufactured primarily in Fibre Reinforced Plastic (FRP) or Mild Steel (MS) with GI sheet cladding, and are available in Indian-style, Western-style, urinal, and combined bathroom configurations. Units are designed as lift-and-shift structures — transportable by trailer — and are equipped with inbuilt sewer connections or holding tanks, overhead water tanks, electrical fittings, and ventilation systems. They are sold as individual cabin units or as multi-seat toilet blocks to construction contractors, infrastructure project operators, and government agencies.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, 'Bunk House Portable Toilets' is a recognised product sub-type within the broader portable toilet / prefabricated cabin category, specifically denoting toilet cabin units deployed at construction labour camps and temporary worker bunk house settlements. The dominant construction materials are FRP (Fibre Reinforced Plastic) and MS (Mild Steel), with GI sheet and PVC as secondary options; FRP is preferred for lightweight, corrosion-resistant single-unit cabins while MS is used for larger, more durable multi-unit blocks. Units are available in Indian-style (squat pan), Western-style (commode), urinal, and combined toilet-bathroom configurations, with standard single-unit dimensions typically in the range of 3×3 ft to 4×4 ft footprint and 7–8.5 ft height. Key structural features include inbuilt sewer systems or holding tanks, overhead water tanks, electrical fittings, ventilation, and lift-and-shift trailer-transportable frames. Multi-seat toilet blocks (2–10 seats) are also common for larger labour camps. Manufacturing hubs are concentrated in Maharashtra (Pune, Mumbai, Thane, Raigad), Gujarat (Ahmedabad, Vadodara), Uttar Pradesh (Ghaziabad), and Delhi NCR. The primary buyers are construction contractors, EPC companies, government infrastructure agencies (NHAI, CPWD, state PWDs), and industrial plant operators. Bio-digester variants are increasingly specified for projects in areas without drainage infrastructure.
